title: Record who occupied which bed, and when, as data rather than as a sentence
description:
Foundation for LODGY-92 and LODGY-93, and it has to land first because neither of those can be built honestly without it.

THE PROBLEM, CONFIRMED IN CODE AND AGAINST LIVE DATA. A tenancy has exactly one bedId, and TenancyAgreementRepository.transferBed does `agreement.copy(bedId = newBedId)` - the previous bed is overwritten and gone. That was the right call for LODGY-34 (a transfer must not split one tenant's payment history into two tenancies) but it means the app cannot answer 'who has lived in this bed'.

On the current test data the database says Suresh is in 102/Bed B and Ramesh Kumar in 102/Bed A. Both of them actually lived in 101/Bed A first. The only record of that is two free-text tenant notes reading 'Moved from Room 101 . Bed A to Room 102 . Bed A.' - English prose, written for a human, not queryable, not translated, and carrying no dates. Ask today's data who has occupied 101/Bed A and the answer is one tenant when the truth is three.

WHAT TO BUILD: occupancy as periods. A row per (tenancy, bed) span with a start and an open-ended finish - a transfer closes the current row and opens a new one, checkout closes it, onboarding opens the first one. The tenancy keeps its bedId as the current bed so nothing that reads it today has to change; the new table is what makes the past answerable.

DO NOT solve this by closing and reopening the agreement on transfer. That is exactly what LODGY-34 rejected, and for a good reason - invoices and payments are keyed to the agreement, so splitting it splits the tenant's money history in half.

THE DECISION THE PO MUST MAKE, because it decides whether the feature tells the truth: what happens to tenancies that already exist. All we know about them is their CURRENT bed plus move-in and move-out - not when any transfer happened. So a backfill can only write one period per agreement at the current bed, which is simply false for anyone who has ever moved: it would place Suresh in 102/Bed B from his move-in date, and a bed-history screen would state that confidently. Three options: (a) backfill one period per agreement and mark it reconstructed, so the UI can distinguish 'recorded' from 'inferred'; (b) backfill nothing and let history begin at the ship date, which is truthful but makes every existing tenant look like they have no past; (c) backfill unmarked, which is the only one that actively lies. RECOMMEND (a). It is the same trade LODGY-52 faced and declined once already - there, the honest answer was to label the occupancy figure rather than fabricate the data behind it.

WORTH KNOWING: this table is also the thing DESIGN.md's roadmap item 6 has been waiting for. LODGY-52 investigated a true past-period occupancy figure, found it needed bed-state history, and settled for labelling the report 'Occupancy (today)' instead. Once occupancy is recorded as periods, that figure becomes computable for real. Not in this ticket's scope - but the PO should know the bill is being paid for two things.
acceptanceCriteria: Onboarding, transfer and checkout each leave a correct, closed-or-open occupancy period behind them
A transfer produces two periods for one tenancy - the old bed closed at the move, the new bed opened - and the tenancy itself is still a single unbroken agreement
Asking which tenants have occupied a given bed returns everyone who did, including those who transferred away from it
The migration is a real one tested against a populated database from the previous version, and no existing screen changes behaviour
The PO's decision on existing tenancies is recorded before the migration is written, and whatever is backfilled can be told apart from what was genuinely recorded
A non-revenue tenancy (warden or caretaker room) is recorded the same way - it is real occupancy, it just bills nobody
Periods never overlap for one bed: a bed cannot be occupied by two tenancies at the same instant

history.note: Filed from a user request for tenant and bed history. Checked in code and against the live database before filing: transferBed overwrites bedId, so the bed half of that request cannot be built truthfully on today's schema - a bed-history screen would silently omit anyone who transferred away. This ticket is the data those two views need. Raised High because LODGY-92 and LODGY-93 are both blocked on it, not because the table is urgent by itself.

THE OPEN DECISION IN THIS TICKET IS NOW ANSWERED BY LODGY-94, which adds a way for the warden to enter past stays themselves. Given that, this ticket should BACKFILL NOTHING automatically - option (b) of the three listed above. The reasoning that made option (a) the recommendation was that an empty history makes every existing tenant look like they have no past; if the warden can fill it with what actually happened, the app guessing at it is strictly worse. A period inferred from the current bed would place a transferred tenant at the wrong bed since their move-in date, and no flag makes that useful. 

ALSO FROM LODGY-94, AND IT MAY CHANGE THIS TABLE'S SHAPE, so please settle it before writing the migration: a stay being backfilled may belong to a tenant who left before the app existed and has no tenancy agreement. If an occupancy period must reference a TENANCY, the backfill has to invent a closed agreement with rent and deposit figures nobody remembers. Letting a period reference the tenant directly, with the tenancy optional, avoids that and costs little now - and considerably more if the table has to be migrated twice.
Starting - building occupancy_periods per the PO's settled decisions: no automatic backfill, tenantId required, tenancyAgreementId nullable. Schema v7 -> v8.

Built: OccupancyPeriod entity, OccupancyPeriodDao and OccupancyPeriodRepository (app/src/main/java/com/lodgy/app/data/{entity,dao,repository}/OccupancyPeriod*.kt), MIGRATION_7_8 (Migrations.kt), LodgyDatabase bumped to v8, DatabaseModule wired. TenancyAgreementRepository.create/transferBed/close now open/close periods (occupancy_periods.tenancyAgreementId nullable per the PO's decision) - every onboarding path (bed grid, agreement form) and transfer/checkout goes through these three methods, so no UI code changed. No backfill migration, as decided. Docs updated: DESIGN.md section 3 + decision log + roadmap item 6, DATA-MODEL.md ERD/delete diagram/notes. Unit tests: TenancyAgreementRepositoryTest extended, new OccupancyPeriodRepositoryTest - 578 tests pass, 0 failures, line coverage 95.9% (gate 0.93). assembleDebug succeeds. FLAG FOR TESTER: the migration was NOT verified against a populated device database - the emulator in this environment failed to boot (stalled post-boot-animation after 15+ min on two separate launches, even after fixing a missing AVD .ini file) and the user chose to proceed without it. Please run the migration against a real pre-v8 database pulled off a device before this ships, per CLAUDE.md's standing migration-testing requirement.

Migration verification requested on LODGY-91/92/93/94 is done. Built the 0.4.0-released code (schema v7) in a separate worktree, installed it on a real emulator, and seeded a populated database directly via the on-device sqlite3 binary (run-as, not the UI) with 1 hostel, 3 rooms, 5 beds, 5 tenants (one closed, one non-revenue) and 5 tenancy agreements. Force-stopped, installed this branch's build over it (adb install -r, same as a warden updating in place), and opened the app: MIGRATION_7_8 and MIGRATION_8_9 both ran, PRAGMA user_version reads 9, occupancy_periods exists with exactly the migration's columns including backfilled, and every pre-existing row survived untouched (counts unchanged) with occupancy_periods correctly empty - no backfill, as decided. Then exercised the app on the upgraded data: bed history correctly said "Never occupied" rather than fabricating a period for the pre-migration tenant, tenant profile duration rendered correctly, and a live transfer through the UI wrote a real occupancy_period (open() fired; close() was a documented no-op since no prior period existed for a tenancy seeded outside the app). No crash in the Lodgy process at any point. This clears the flag raised when LODGY-91/92/93/94 moved to Testing.

PASS - verified all 7 acceptance criteria on-device against real app-driven data (not just seeded rows), on top of the migration verification already recorded. Onboarded a tenant through the UI and confirmed onboarding opens a period; transferred an app-onboarded tenant a second time and confirmed the SAME tenancyAgreementId now carries two periods - the old bed closed at the move, the new bed opened, tenancy unbroken (AC2, the ticket's central claim). Checked the tenant out and confirmed the period closed. observeByBedId returns a transferred-away tenant's closed period alongside the current one (AC3). Migration + backfilled-vs-recorded distinction already verified (AC4, AC5). Onboarded a warden/caretaker room (non-revenue) through the bed sheet shortcut and confirmed it opens a period exactly like a revenue tenancy and shows in bed history (AC6). AC7 (no overlap) holds structurally: onboarding and transfer only ever offer VACANT beds (BedPickerViewModel.getVacantChoices, TransferViewModel.getVacantBedsByHostel), so the live open()/close() path can't create two tenancies on one bed in normal use, even though OccupancyPeriodRepository.open() itself has no defensive overlap check (only backfill()/editBackfilled() check) - worth knowing if that upstream vacant-only gating is ever relaxed, but not a defect today. No regressions found in existing screens.
